run.question: In Loki, run the query `{service="checkout"}` against namespace app-282 and tell me how many error-level log lines come back. If the selector returns nothing, find the right one.

report.summary: The query as written, `{service="checkout"}`, matched nothing in Loki; because that view returned status no_data it is recorded as a gap rather than as a fact, so the answer to the literal query is "nothing returned" and no error count can be taken from it. The selector that actually matches this workload is `{namespace="app-282", acme_service="checkout"}` (streams also carry job="checkout-logs", filename="/var/log/checkout.log", level and pod="checkout-698c8f5df-8q5h7"; there is no `service` label). Against that selector, 4 ERROR-level log lines are present in the tool's last-hour window (2026-11-23T18:11:02Z–19:11:02Z), alongside 10 INFO and 2 WARN lines. The same aggregate over the full authorized 30-day window returns the identical breakdown (ERROR 4, INFO 10, WARN 2), i.e. the only checkout log lines Loki holds for that window are the single burst at 2026-11-23T19:10:27Z on pod checkout-698c8f5df-8q5h7. The 4 ERROR lines are: "Webhook delivery exhausted retries for partner ACME", "Order persistence failed: deadlock on orders table", "Inventory check timed out for SKU-77481", "Payment processor refused: invalid token (txn 9d1f)". No root cause is assigned: this was a log-count question, not an incident investigation, and the errors were not traced to any dependency.

claims.text: Loki labels for the checkout workload in namespace app-282 are acme_service="checkout", job="checkout-logs", filename="/var/log/checkout.log", namespace="app-282", pod="checkout-698c8f5df-8q5h7" plus a level label; there is no `service` label, so the working selector is `{namespace="app-282", acme_service="checkout"}`.

`sum by (level) (count_over_time({namespace="app-282", acme_service="checkout"}[1h]))` evaluated at 2026-11-23T19:11:02Z returns level=ERROR 4, level=INFO 10, level=WARN 2 — exactly 4 error-level log lines in the last-hour window 2026-11-23T18:11:02Z–19:11:02Z.

The same aggregate over the full authorized 30-day window (2026-10-24T19:11:02Z–2026-11-23T19:11:02Z, range 30d) returns the identical breakdown ERROR 4, INFO 10, WARN 2, so no additional checkout error lines exist in Loki for that wider window.

The four ERROR lines returned for pod checkout-698c8f5df-8q5h7 at 2026-11-23T19:10:27.71Z read: "Payment processor refused: invalid token (txn 9d1f)", "Inventory check timed out for SKU-77481", "Order persistence failed: deadlock on orders table", "Webhook delivery exhausted retries for partner ACME"; the same burst contains 2 WARN lines (rate limiter near threshold for /v1/checkout; slow database response from orders_db 1.2s) and 10 INFO "Checkout flow completed" lines.

gaps: The literal selector `{service="checkout"}` was queried for 2026-11-23T18:11:02Z–19:11:02Z and the view returned status no_data with zero lines; that view cannot support a fact, so it is only recorded that this query matched nothing in that window, not that checkout logged no errors under that label scheme.
The 4-error count comes from the corrected selector `{namespace="app-282", acme_service="checkout"}`, not from the query as originally written.

Loki line retrieval shows only the newest lines up to the tool limit, and retention, ingest delay, label selection and line filters can leave gaps; the 16 lines seen are the only checkout lines returned for the window.
I did not page through individual log lines day by day across the 30-day window; that figure rests on a single aggregate count_over_time evaluation.
I did not read the pod's Kubernetes status, events or container termination reasons, nor the previous container's logs, so nothing is concluded about pod health or restarts.
I did not investigate the four error messages further in traces or in the downstream services (payment, inventory, orders database, partner webhook), so no cause or downstream impact is established.
next_steps: If an error trend is needed rather than a single total, run count_over_time with a short range (e.g. [5m]) per step over the incident period to locate when the ERROR burst began.

If the four error messages are to be attributed, check traces/traces_search for checkout spans with error status around 2026-11-23T19:10 and the dependency operations they call, plus those services' own error metrics.
